title: Rejoice, Ye Righteous, in the Lord
description: Rejoice, Ye Righteous, in the Lord in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 33, part 1, headed “Works of creation and providence”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Re-joice, ye right-eous, in the Lord, This work be-longs to you: Sing of his name, his ways, his word, How ho-ly, just, and true!

lines: Rejoice, ye righteous, in the Lord,
Sing of his name, his ways, his word,
His works of nature and of grace
And by the Spirit of the Lord
He bid the liquid waters flow
The flowing seas their limits know,
Ye tenants of the spacious earth,
He spake, and nature took its birth,
He scorns the angry nations' rage,
His counsel stands thro' every age,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
